The game caters to Alien fans with there being movie references and fan service 
the game is fun but feels like its missing something . doesnt really do anything new doesnt really have any scare moments or fear of dread that Aliens is know for and kinda comes off to me as Helldivers 2 Aliens 

The AI is really dumb and rail shooter . They spawn out one hole in the wall you just stand in front of spraying until they stop coming out they move from spawn point directly in a straight line to you with the occasional one hiding around a corner at a T junction ready to jump on your face and pin you down 

It is fun but would be a bargin bin game get for a cheap special and have the few fun hours the game offers

If you get this game on sale, it's 100% worth it. A good amount of content for you (and friends!) to burn through.
Weapons are diverse and fun, classes are equally diverse and fun. Enemies variety and difficulty is very well balanced in my opinion.
The only downside I can think of, as of writing this, is the price point of the game & DLC in relation to the content you get... Which is resolved by buying the game on sale. Buying this at full price is NOT worth it. 50% off or more and it's a fantastic grab!

I waited several years to get this game and it has been fun!  The team did a great job bringing it to life...from the aesthetics of the game down to the sounds of the weaponry.   The weapon/upgrade system is enough to keep you aspiring to do more.

tl;dr: It is a very good time getting up to shenanigans in space with your mates. Highly recommend.

I'm not normally one for multiplayer games; adulthood makes it hard to find people to play with reliably and on the higher difficulties, this game Demands a coordinated team. Lower difficulties are a great time if you're here for a power fantasy, but if you want to feel like a Colonial Marine, the harder the better. Luckily, there is still a modest community active and they have a Discord and everything. I met some real nice folks doing that and I'm always worried when jumping into a game with an established player-base that a new player will be looked down on. Not so here. Very welcoming place, so if you held off playing for that reason, rest assured.

I also do not typically like games with rogue-like elements, and this does require you to replay the same levels a lot if you want to make honest power progression which is... kiiiind of like a rogue-like. But it's got a decent story to it as well, with a cast of characters who vary from Just There (Herrera), to Extremely Annoying (that's you, Hoenikker), to adorably weird (Esther). Frankly, this helped a lot. So if you're wondering if you'll be bored replaying the same missions over and over... maybe. Grain of salt there. But I am notoriously bad at those things and loved every second.

Difficulty increases cause, yes, the enemies to take more hits before dying and to dish out more in return, but there are also some fun (and punishing) mechanics that are only on the higher difficulties also (that I won't spoil because they're absolutely worth experiencing the first time for yourself).

The gameplay itself is quite good. There are a variety of enemies to keep things interesting and some of the spawns are random which provides some measure of variety on replays. If you're into Alien lore, there's loads of that too; some nice callbacks (not ham-fisted, some subtle and some just nods, it was good). There's a wide armoury to select from and while some of them are different only on technicalities, most of them were distinct enough that I found it completely worthwhile to try out a bunch and see which gelled best with my personal preferences. Sometimes this was because of bullet spread, accuracy, how quickly it reloads, or - in one or two notable instances - the way it sounded when shooting just REALLY grated on my ears. Can't stand those two guns. There are eight classes with unique ability kits, from your dps classes to a tank and two supports. But even within those roles, they are distinct and you cannot sub out one dps for another. They have specialised roles and work best when utilised to that end. Of course, demolisher has rockets. So. Xenos go boom. Very satisfying.

The designs of the xenomorphs, the environments, the audio was all spot on. This is to Aliens (the 1986 movie) what Alien: Isolation is to Alien (1979).

Customisation of your marine isn't the Most Exhaustable ever, but you unlock plenty of cosmetics and can make your guns fancy and that's fun. It took me 120hrs to 100% the achievements but there's still loads left to do and you can bet I'm going to keep coming back for it. Those Quake decals from the extreme difficulty will be mine...
